links.outcome: General-purpose ChatGPT accuracy for predicting cut-out from radiographs and clinical data
links.effect: Sensitivity 68.0%, specificity 62.7%, PPV 4.5%, AUC 0.694; 360 false positives vs 8 false negatives; judged clinically insufficient.
links.quote: ChatGPT demonstrated limited, clinically insufficient accuracy for predicting cut-out following proximal femoral nailing, with a prohibitive false-positive burden and inverted calibration.

links.outcome: Calibration of ChatGPT predicted probabilities for correct versus incorrect classifications
links.effect: Calibration inverted: median predicted probability 9% for correct vs 40% for incorrect classifications (Mann-Whitney p < 0.001).
links.quote: Calibration was inverted: the median predicted probability was lower for correct (9%) than for incorrect (40%) classifications (Mann-Whitney p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Model performance by implant subgroup (TFNA vs Gamma nail)
links.effect: TFNA sensitivity 73.7%, AUC 0.730 vs Gamma nail sensitivity 50.0%, AUC 0.606; difference not statistically significant.
links.quote: Performance was higher for TFNA (sensitivity 73.7%, AUC 0.730) than for Gamma nail (sensitivity 50.0%, AUC 0.606).

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the predictive/diagnostic accuracy and calibration of a multimodal foundation model (ChatGPT) on retrospective clinical and radiographic data, without testing a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
